instantiated_cells.justification: State agencies that file a statement under § 13.695 are expressly not subject to the principal/lobbyist licensing and registration provisions, indicating executive-branch agencies are not required to register as lobbyists under this subchapter.

The governor is an "elective state official," and § 13.621(3) provides that an elective state official is not subject to the lobbying registration/licensing provisions when acting in an official capacity.

Entities that are "agencies" (defined broadly to include boards/commissions/departments) are covered by the agency statement regime in § 13.695 and, under § 13.621(2), are not subject to the lobbyist/principal registration and licensing requirements (except as provided in § 13.695).

The subchapter does not apply to "lobbying of an agency official by an agency official of a different agency or another agency official of the same agency," so government agencies lobbying other agencies are exempt from registration.

Section 13.621(3) exempts an "employee of the legislature" (and elective state officials) from the lobbying registration/licensing provisions when acting in an official capacity, so the legislative branch is not required to register as lobbyists for official activities.

An individual paid by a principal to lobby is a "lobbyist" and § 13.66 prohibits engaging in lobbying as a lobbyist unless licensed and authorized, which applies to lobbying firms’ lobbyist employees/contractors.

A "principal" is any person who employs a lobbyist, and § 13.64(1) requires every principal exceeding $500 in lobbying expenditures/obligations to file a registration statement, which can include local governmental units when they employ lobbyists.
Section 13.66 states no person may engage in lobbying as a lobbyist unless licensed under § 13.63 and authorized under § 13.65, making lobbyist registration/licensing legally required.

A principal is defined as a person who employs a lobbyist, and § 13.64(1) requires every such principal (once exceeding $500 in a calendar year for nonexempt lobbying) to file a registration statement with the commission.

Because "principal" includes any person who employs a lobbyist and § 13.64(1) mandates registration for principals exceeding $500 in nonexempt lobbying, public entities other than state agencies must register when they employ lobbyists and meet the threshold.

The definition of "lobbyist" requires the individual to be employed by a principal or receive economic consideration (other than reimbursement for actual expenses), so purely volunteer lobbyists are not required to be licensed/registered as lobbyists.
